forces.title: AI-driven personalization to boost streaming engagement and retention.
forces.description: Video streaming platforms can leverage advanced AI, specifically contextual bandit algorithms, to deliver true one-to-one personalization. This optimizes subscriber interactions in real-time, tailoring content recommendations, offers, and re-engagement campaigns based on individual behavior, preferences, and lifecycle stage. Such targeted approaches are crucial for strengthening subscriber relationships, improving retention, and deepening engagement.

forces.title: AI transforms film and TV content creation, enabling new formats.
forces.description: Artificial intelligence is fundamentally altering the film and TV production landscape, streamlining processes from script to screen. This transformation not only compresses timelines and automates workflows but also facilitates the emergence of entirely new content formats and innovative distribution models. These AI-enabled advancements contribute to a more diverse and potentially higher volume of content available for streaming platforms.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: AI streamlines film and TV production workflows.
forces.description: AI is being integrated across the entire film and TV production pipeline, from script breakdown and storyboarding in preproduction to dubbing, subtitling, and match cutting in postproduction. This 'AI-first' approach is leading to significant productivity improvements (e.g., 5-10% in preproduction) by automating manual tasks like rush logging and enhancing visualization. These efficiencies can result in faster content delivery and potentially more diverse content for streaming platforms.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: AI democratizes filmmaking, benefiting consumers and major distributors.
forces.description: AI's low cost of entry, often a low double-digit dollar monthly subscription, democratizes filmmaking by making professional-grade content creation accessible to a wider range of creators. Simultaneously, power is concentrating with major distributors, with five global players commanding a majority of content spend. This dynamic may lead to a 'hollowing out of the middle,' with a focus on top-end premium storytelling and a long tail of grassroots content, ultimately offering consumers more choices at better prices.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: AI adoption significantly reduces content production costs for studios.
forces.description: Proactive film and TV studios can realize approximately 30 percent reduction in effort for equivalent content production by embracing AI technologies. This substantial efficiency gain acts as a major productivity lever, allowing studios to either reinvest savings into more ambitious projects, increase content output, or secure market share through cost-effective content delivery, directly benefiting streaming platforms with a more robust content supply.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: Audience/creative rejection and IP infringement pose AI risks.
forces.description: The adoption of AI in film and TV faces significant challenges from potential audience rejection of AI-generated content and strong resistance from creative communities, as demonstrated by labor strikes. Additionally, widespread concerns exist regarding IP and rights infringement, as AI models are often trained on copyrighted material. These factors introduce considerable risk and potential barriers to the seamless integration and acceptance of AI in content creation for streaming.
forces.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

forces.title: Rising energy costs pressure media infrastructure, impacting streaming margins.
forces.description: The TMT sector, particularly media infrastructure like data centers essential for streaming platforms, faces indirect pressure from significantly increased energy costs due to geopolitical instability. As energy is a core cost input for these operations, rising prices erode profit margins and can lead to delays in investment decisions, potentially hindering the expansion and operational efficiency of streaming services in Ireland.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Elevated cybersecurity risk threatens digital infrastructure of streaming.
forces.description: Geopolitical instability has heightened cybersecurity threats, impacting digital infrastructure across various sectors, including media. Streaming platforms, relying heavily on robust online systems, face increased operational and reputational risks from cyber-attacks. Irish organizations are responding by re-evaluating critical infrastructure locations and increasing cyber insurance, underscoring a broader need for enhanced resilience planning in the digital entertainment space.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Favorable Irish policies boost media content production for streaming.
forces.description: Ireland's supportive policy frameworks, including the Section 481 tax relief and the Visual Effects (VFX) Uplift, are significantly stimulating media content production. These incentives attract international projects, such as Netflix and Amazon Prime Video series, and increase local production spend. Such favorable conditions ensure a robust supply of high-quality content, acting as a strong tailwind for streaming platforms operating in or sourcing content from Ireland.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: AI poised to offer consumers broader content choices and lower prices.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey experts Jamie Vickers and Alec Wrubel express a positive outlook on AI's long-term impact on consumers within the film and TV industry. They anticipate that AI will lead to a wider array of content choices and potentially more affordable pricing. This benefit stems from AI's ability to democratize filmmaking by reducing production costs and facilitating new content formats, although it is acknowledged that this might coincide with a concentration of power among major content distributors.
viewpoints.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV

demand_drivers.description: Global streaming platforms and other media entities are driving demand for production, choosing Ireland as a location due to its supportive environment.
Government incentives like Section 481 tax relief and VFX Uplift attract significant investment and international productions, bolstering local spend.

market_sizing.methodology: Total production spend in Ireland's media sector, reported as €544 million in 2025, showing a 26% year-on-year increase. This figure reflects strong international demand and the impact of favorable policy frameworks, including tax relief for international and VFX productions (e.g., Netflix, Amazon Prime Video).
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

new_opportunities.description: AI could enable the development of entirely novel content types and distribution pathways, similar to how Netflix evolved beyond DVD. This unlocks significant revenue potential through innovation in storytelling and audience engagement within the streaming industry.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Creation of new content formats and distribution channels

market_sizing.methodology: Forecast of global revenue potential that could be redistributed over five years (from 2026), driven by the transformation of the film and TV industry through AI adoption, including new content formats and distribution channels. This figure represents the economic shift and new value creation due to AI.
market_sizing.source_title: Lights, camera, algorithm: How AI is rewriting the rules of film and TV
